title: Introduction & Host Banter
summary: Wes Bos and Scott Tolinski introduce the episode, chatting about Chrome’s new Dev Tools MCP Server. Scott also shares a funny story about chipping his tooth during a previous recording.

title: Community Announcements
summary: The hosts announce an upcoming meetup in San Francisco on October 27 and invite developers to submit their scariest ‘spooky’ web-development mistakes for the annual Halloween episode.

title: Understanding Chrome’s MCP Server
summary: They explain what the new MCP Server is — an AI-driven interface that allows programmatic control of Chrome DevTools. The discussion covers how MCP extends AI models with tools for debugging, inspecting pages, and fetching data.

title: Automating Workflows with MCP
summary: The hosts explore how MCP can automate browser actions similarly to Playwright or Puppeteer. They discuss potential use cases like debugging, testing, and developing real-time feedback loops.

title: Integrating Figma and Multi-Tool MCPs
summary: They imagine connecting multiple MCP servers — for instance, using Figma’s MCP to convert a design into code, compare screenshots, and verify layouts automatically. This highlights the ecosystem potential of connected MCP tools.

title: Sponsor Segment: Sentry MCP
summary: A short sponsor break featuring Sentry’s MCP integration and its AI assistant ‘Sear,’ which can automatically diagnose hard-to-find bugs by analyzing logs and environment variables.

title: Setup, Security & Technical Design
summary: Wes explains that Chrome launches a new isolated instance for MCP interactions to prevent malicious access. They walk through configuring MCP servers in VS Code or via NPX, emphasizing security and sandboxing.

title: Debugging, Console Errors & Performance
summary: Scott demonstrates how MCP can visit a localhost app, capture console errors, and even suggest fixes. They discuss automating debugging, performance checks, and console integrations directly from chat interfaces.

title: Closing Thoughts & Future of DevTools AI
summary: They wrap up reflecting on AI-powered DevTools, Chrome’s new AI insights, and how the future of web development may blend traditional coding with intelligent, browser-based automation.
